changes.text_diff:
@@ -27,6 +27,8 @@
 
 By default (durable: false) the job lives only in this Claude session — nothing is written to disk, and the job is gone when Claude exits.
 Pass durable: true to write to .claude/scheduled_tasks.json so the job survives restarts.
+If Claude Code can't tell which organization this session is signed in to, the job stays session-only even with durable: true.
+If the result says "Session-only" after durable: true, tell the user that the job won't survive restarts.
 Only use durable: true when the user explicitly asks for the task to persist ("keep doing this every day", "set this up permanently").

@@ -37,13 +39,13 @@
 ## Runtime behavior
 
 Jobs only fire while the REPL is idle (not mid-query).
-Durable jobs persist to .claude/scheduled_tasks.json and survive session restarts — on next launch they resume automatically.
+Durable jobs that were saved to .claude/scheduled_tasks.json survive session restarts — on the next launch signed in to the same organization they resume automatically.
 One-shot durable tasks that were missed while the REPL was closed are surfaced for catch-up.
 Session-only jobs die with the process.
 The scheduler shifts each job by a fixed per-job offset on top of whatever you pick: by default a recurring job runs up to 50% of its period late (max 30 min), and a one-shot job landing on :00 or :30 runs up to 90 s early.
 The result of this tool and of CronList gives each job's actual next run time: when you tell the user when a job will run, give that time, not the minute in the cron expression.
 Picking an off-minute is still the bigger lever.
 
-Recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days — they fire one final time, then are deleted. This bounds session lifetime. Tell the user about the 7-day limit when scheduling recurring jobs.
+Recurring tasks auto-expire after 30 days — they fire one final time, with a note that it is their last run, then are deleted. This bounds session lifetime. Tell the user about the 30-day limit when scheduling recurring jobs.

after.description: Claude desktop app only. Where your allow list and deny list apply to MCP servers added in the Claude desktop app. "code" (default): Your allow list also governs MCP servers added in the Claude desktop app, in Code tab sessions and the Artifact pane. "all": Your allow list and your deny list also govern MCP servers added in the Claude desktop app, in every tab (including Chat and Cowork). "off": Your allow list doesn't govern MCP servers added in the Claude desktop app. Read only from managed settings. Any other value counts as `all`. Where sources are merged or mixed, `off` counts as `all`. Leave the key out, or set it only in the managed source that holds your list. `deniedMcpServers` applies in Code tab sessions and the Artifact pane with every value, and in every tab with `all`. MCP servers sent to SSH hosts are not governed by these lists in this release. The Claude Code CLI reads nothing from this key, but written alone in a higher managed source it makes that source lead, and Claude Code skips the managed sources beneath it. Write it only beside the list it scopes.

When true in managed settings, Claude Code lists and loads no skill of an MCP server that it connects to directly, reads no listed file of a loaded one, and lists no directory of the server. On the Team and Enterprise plans these skills are off unless an administrator sets it to false. Connectors that Claude Code reaches through Anthropic keep their skills, and each server keeps its tools. In a user, project or local settings file it has no effect.
